the 1/4 BPS Wilson loop is a perfect tool for testing and developing the localization technique.
the 1/4 BPS Wilson loop is a perfect match with the localization computation, and that the 1 BPS and 1/2BPS Wilson loop have a framing factor that matches the one proposed from localization.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that the Wilson loops in Chern-Simons theories are well defined objects in the presence of supersymmetric defects, and that the localization method is a powerful tool to compute them.
we have provided the first evidence that the 1/4 BPS Wilson loop can be used as a probe for the 1/8 BPS partition function.
we provide the first evidence that ABJM theory is indeed a topological field theory.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have found a concrete example where the proposed framing factor works.
the 1/ 2 BPS Wilson loops in ABJM theory are not anomalous, in the sense that the two loops correction is not proportional to a power of the 't Hooft coupling.
we have provided a concrete example of how the localization formula for the 1/8 BPS partition function can be used to compute the expectation value for 1/2 supersymmetric observables.
